title: Distinguish unknown mailbox receipts from receipts issued to another participant or mailbox
outcome: Mailbox receipt rejections distinguish an unknown token from a token issued to another participant or mailbox, preserve cursors, and retain exact-receipt acceptance. The reported 06:14Z rejection is documented as a caller transcription error, not an identical retry or storage race.
acceptance: The 06:14Z incident's root cause is recorded with original transcript line references: the failed acknowledge transposed abd2 to ab2d; the successful acknowledge used the original issued receipt.

An unknown receipt and an existing receipt belonging to another participant or mailbox produce distinct typed errors without moving any cursor; the exact original receipt is subsequently accepted, including across separate connections to the same store.
A delegation-MCP bridge regression verifies that mailbox reads and acknowledgements forward the same serving session identity and preserve the exact supplied receipt.
The focused receipt regressions and full gate pass on the final input, and an independent read-only review pair has no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
